result.detail: 5 objection(s): Each claimed cause is critiqued for missing controls, unsupported quantitative claims, or insufficient evidence from the provided SHA256 records.

objections.claim: FY2018 contains 322 duplicate rows across 7 source tables
Apple Inc. 11 Revenues facts in 2018 contributed $1205.3B of the jump
Corrected Manufacturing is 1.125x ($49.6B) representing 3.8% of the reported jump
Tesla, Inc. grew 1.737x FY2017 to FY2018 and contributed $55.9B (4.3% of jump)
No ingestion gap exists because Zetaris holds 11 Apple facts and SEC endpoint returns 11

args.question: is the FY2018 jump real?
args.finding:
Verdict: MIXED (filing_year_duplication=96.2%, real_change=3.8%)
- FY2018 holds 100 rows across 32 distinct period_end dates; 322 duplicate rows across the 7 source tables.
- Apple Inc. has 11 Revenues facts, all in fiscal_year 2018; that contributes $1205.3B of the $1295.0B jump. Target Corporation has no Revenues fact after fiscal_year 2014. Scout found the replacement concept RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax with 9 annual 10-K facts.
- Corrected Manufacturing is 1.125x ($49.6B); that is 3.8% of the reported jump. SEC frames parity 12/12.
- Tesla, Inc. is the fastest-growing filer in Manufacturing (1.737x FY2017 to FY2018), but its $55.9B is only 4.3% of the reported jump.
- Zetaris holds 11 Apple Inc. facts; the SEC companyconcept endpoint returns 11. Nothing is missing.
Note: concept_switch_missing_history is confirmed as a data-quality finding but carries no separate share: deduplicating to one annual fact per (cik, period_end) recovers Apple Inc. and Target Corporation's prior-year facts, so it does not add to the reported jump.
Note: Eliminated with exhibits, not left as possibilities: single_filer_growth, ingestion_gap.
Note: Defense Counsel raised 5 objection(s); the deterministic code gate is final.

statements: CREATE SCHEMASTORE CONTAINER exhibit_a_shadow

CREATE OR REPLACE SCHEMASTORE VIEW sector_revenue_by_year WITH CONTAINER exhibit_a_shadow AS WITH annual AS (
  SELECT
    s.sic_division,
    f.cik,
    f.period_start,
    f.period_end,
    f.value_usd,
    f.filed_date,
    CASE
      WHEN MONTH(f.period_end) <= 6 THEN YEAR(f.period_end) - 1
      ELSE YEAR(f.period_end)
    END AS period_year,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
      PARTITION BY f.cik, f.period_end
      ORDER BY f.filed_date DESC, f.value_usd DESC
    ) AS rn
  FROM (
    SELECT * FROM edgar.apple_revenue_table
    UNION ALL SELECT * FROM edgar.ibm_revenue_table
    UNION ALL SELECT * FROM edgar.oracle_revenue_table
    UNION ALL SELECT * FROM edgar.walmart_revenue_table
    UNION ALL SELECT * FROM edgar.target_revenue_table
    UNION ALL SELECT * FROM edgar.ford_revenue_table
    UNION ALL SELECT * FROM edgar.tesla_revenue_table
  ) f
  LEFT JOIN edgar.sic_edgar_usl s ON s.cik = f.cik
  WHERE DATEDIFF(f.period_end, f.period_start) BETWEEN 330 AND 400
)
SELECT
  sic_division,
  period_year AS fiscal_year,
  SUM(value_usd) AS revenue_usd
FROM annual
WHERE rn = 1
  AND period_year BETWEEN 2016 AND 2019
GROUP BY sic_division, period_year

hypotheses.statement: The 2018 movement in Manufacturing is inflated because analytics.sector_revenue_by_year sums value_usd grouped by the filing's fiscal_year, so prior-year comparatives, quarterly facts and year-to-date facts are counted again under the later filing year.
hypotheses.note: FY2018 holds 100 rows across 32 distinct period_end dates; 322 duplicate rows across the 7 source tables.

hypotheses.statement: The 2018 bucket gains a filer that is absent from 2017, because a filer's Revenues concept stops after one filing and its whole fact history lands in a single fiscal_year.
hypotheses.note: Apple Inc. has 11 Revenues facts, all in fiscal_year 2018; that contributes $1205.3B of the $1295.0B jump. Target Corporation has no Revenues fact after fiscal_year 2014. Scout found the replacement concept RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax with 9 annual 10-K facts.

hypotheses.statement: Revenue in Manufacturing genuinely grew between 2017 and 2018; the increase should survive deduplication and agree with an independent SEC frames value.
hypotheses.note: Corrected Manufacturing is 1.125x ($49.6B); that is 3.8% of the reported jump. SEC frames parity 12/12.

hypotheses.statement: One fast-growing filer in Manufacturing explains the 2018 movement on its own.
hypotheses.note: Tesla, Inc. is the fastest-growing filer in Manufacturing (1.737x FY2017 to FY2018), but its $55.9B is only 4.3% of the reported jump.

hypotheses.statement: The artifact is an ingestion gap: Zetaris lost facts that the SEC endpoint still returns, so the naive series is missing rows rather than duplicating them.
hypotheses.note: Zetaris holds 11 Apple Inc. facts; the SEC companyconcept endpoint returns 11. Nothing is missing.

discovery.replacement_reason: Revenues has 3 annual 10-K facts ending 2018-09-29; RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax has 9 annual 10-K facts ending 2025-09-27 and a continuous chain, so the missing history is a concept switch, not a lost source.
discovery.rule: revenue concept must have USD annual 10-K facts (330-400 days), a chain ending within 421 days, and extend the stopped concept

critic.detail: 5 objection(s): Each claimed cause is critiqued for missing controls, unsupported quantitative claims, or insufficient evidence from the provided SHA256 records.

objections.claim: FY2018 contains 322 duplicate rows across 7 source tables
Apple Inc. 11 Revenues facts in 2018 contributed $1205.3B of the jump
Corrected Manufacturing is 1.125x ($49.6B) representing 3.8% of the reported jump
Tesla, Inc. grew 1.737x FY2017 to FY2018 and contributed $55.9B (4.3% of jump)
No ingestion gap exists because Zetaris holds 11 Apple facts and SEC endpoint returns 11
